title: Garden — Generative Regime, Resilience and Stewardship
purpose: Define Garden operationally as a regime that protects differentiated life, circulates resources, supports correction and increases independent future capacity.
epistemic_rule: Garden is a project operator. Ecology/resilience research supplies comparators; social or spiritual systems are not literally ecosystems.
core_definition: Garden is not a place of effortless goodness. It is a managed generative regime in which boundaries, diversity, circulation, feedback, pruning, learning and stewardship preserve enough structure for differentiated life to grow without permanent dependency on the center.

required_conditions.question: What must be kept out or regulated so growth is possible without enclosure becoming a Shell?
How do nourishment, information, attention and opportunity circulate rather than pool at one node?
Are there multiple viable capacities/roles so one failure does not collapse the whole?
Can changing conditions and errors be sensed and acted on?
Can the system adapt rather than preserving one form at all costs?
Can affected parts contribute knowledge and correction?
Can participants leave, differentiate or become independent without punitive dependence?
Does the regime produce future autonomous capacity rather than only harvest current output?

regime_contract.anti_pattern: If the center must retain monopoly, extract value, suppress correction or make exit costly in order to survive, the regime is drifting from Garden toward Farm/Shell/Swamp.

findings: Resilience research emphasizes diversity/redundancy, connectivity, slow variables/feedbacks, learning, participation and polycentric governance as recurring resilience principles.
Loss of functional diversity and altered disturbance regimes can reduce resilience and increase the risk of regime shifts.
Resilience includes persistence, adaptation and sometimes transformation rather than simply returning to the old state.
resilience_context.project_use: Garden should preserve the capacity to adapt and renew, not merely preserve one ideal arrangement.

garden_tests.boundary_test: Protection increases viable differentiation without making boundary preservation the supreme goal.
garden_tests.gardener_test: The steward becomes less necessary as others gain competence/capacity.
garden_tests.fruit_test: Outputs nourish, repair or reproduce future capacity without exporting hidden harm.
garden_tests.diversity_test: Difference remains functional rather than being flattened into one identity.
garden_tests.repair_test: Damage can be acknowledged and corrected without destroying the whole or requiring permanent enemy roles.

relations.house: House supplies bounded rooms and Doors; Garden describes whether life inside those boundaries can grow.
relations.tree: Tree is the organism; Garden is the regime around its growth.
relations.fruit: Fruit evaluates what the regime actually produces.
relations.forge: Forge processes damage/candidates; Garden reintegrates useful repaired capacity.
relations.swamp: Swamp is unresolved entanglement; Garden maintains circulation and correction.
